analysis.investment_thesis: Choice International has delivered an impressive 51% net profit CAGR over 9 years from a tiny base (₹4 Cr in FY16 to ₹163 Cr in FY25), but the market has priced this growth with extraordinary generosity at 77x P/E and 16x P/S for a ₹921 Cr revenue financial services firm — even the forward P/E of 48x assumes flawless execution in a hyper-competitive broking and NBFC landscape. The serial negative operating cash flows (only 1/5 years positive OCF) suggest growth is being bought rather than organically generated.
key_strengths: Exceptional growth trajectory: revenue grew from ₹285 Cr (FY22) to ₹921 Cr (FY25) — a near 3x in three years — showing genuine business momentum in broking and NBFC services
Diversified financial services model covering broking, wealth, NBFC, insurance, and advisory provides multiple growth vectors riding India's financialisation theme
ROE of 19.6% and ROCE of 20% show the underlying business returns capital well when not in expansion mode
key_risks: Valuation is unjustifiable at 77x P/E; even at the forward P/E of 48x, this stock requires 30%+ earnings growth compounding for many years just to justify today's price — no margin of safety whatsoever
OCF negative in 4 out of last 5 years with FCF at -₹451 Cr in FY25; the business is cash-consumptive and reliant on external financing (financing CF +₹449 Cr in FY25)
Capital markets broking revenues are highly cyclical — a prolonged market downturn would devastate top-line and the NBFC book adds credit risk in a downturn
red_flags: P/S of 16.1x for a broking-NBFC business is pricing in perfection; Zerodha (unlisted, market leader) earns more profit at a fraction of this market cap relative to revenue
DII ownership of only 0.30% — sophisticated Indian institutional investors have essentially zero conviction in this stock at current prices, which speaks volumes
Consistently negative FCF (-₹451 Cr in FY25) while the company raises ₹449 Cr in financing means the equity story is funded by dilution/debt, not earnings power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I deeply appreciate the India capital markets and wealth management story — it is a multi-decade secular growth theme as household savings shift from gold and real estate to financial assets. Choice International is participating in this theme and the growth numbers are real. However, I have never believed in paying any price for growth, and 77x P/E for a ₹163 Cr net profit business with ₹16,163 Cr market cap is simply paying for hope, not fundamentals.

In competitive financial services — broking, NBFC, insurance distribution — scale and technology moats matter enormously. Choice is competing against Zerodha, Angel, IIFL, and Bajaj Finance, all of which have vastly superior scale. The promoter at 53.66% is adequate but not high-conviction. I would happily revisit this at ₹200-250 Cr net profit and 25-30x P/E, which would represent a far more reasonable entry into what is otherwise an interesting franchise.
